steps.text: Slice the zucchini and yellow squash. Place the sliced vegetables in a large skillet or saucepan with the butter. Saute over a medium-low heat for 10 minutes before seasoning with salt, pepper and dill.
Continue to saute for 10 additional minutes before adding the lemon juice. Stir the vegetables well and remove from heat. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Dill and Butter Squash
raw_recipe.description: This is a different angle on an old veggie. Even the kids will eat this one! If you've got fresh dill in your garden, substitute 2 to 3 fresh sprigs dill for the dried dill weed.
raw_recipe.name: Dill and Butter Squash

review.reviewBody:
Great taste. I made the following changes:
 2 garlic cloves (minced) sauted w/ the zucchini & squash, 1.5 tsp dill, cut back on butter & used some olive oil instead

While I wouldn't call this "a different angle on an old veggie" as the submitter describes, it doesn't take away from the fact that this is just plain simple and good. No need to measure, just saute the squash in butter as needed, add salt, pepper and dill to your taste. I cooked this, however, at medium-high heat, not the medium-low as the recipe directs. Saute as long as necessary to achieve a crisp-tender doneness, not till it's soggy and mushy, which can easily happen with summer squash. Great fresh flavors with just a few simple ingredients - what's not to like?

This is a versatile recipe. You can change it anyway you like. I used fresh lemon for the lemon juice and did it give it a kick. Also, I used fresh dill weed. During the summer months I will vary it some more. Experiment - it's fun!

One of my favorite ways to have summer squash. I've been making it for years. I cook this in layers....first carrots cut on the diagonal, then yellow squash, zucchini, maybe some green peppers, and then mushrooms, shaking dill between each layer. Drizzle some olive oil on top, lots of garlic and about a tablespoon of butter. Cover tightly and just let it cook very slowly, around 20 mins or so, depending on the amount you're cooking and how tender you like your vegies. No need to stir. We also like to put it on top of our fresh pasta. So good!!!

I put a big twist on this one and it was out of this world! I sauteed a large onion, minced garlic and minced ginger in a combination of butter and olive oil. Then, added 4 zucchini and 4 yellow squash, covered and simmered for 10-15 minutes. I then added Lemon Essential Oil, fresh Rosemary, dill weed, freshly ground peppercorn, ground sea salt and a little lemon pepper for good measure and simmered another 5-7 mins. It was so delectable that I, a 5'7" size 4 woman, ate the entire dish with the exception of 1 cup I saved in case my son wanted some when he returned home later. :)

I was suprised by how much I loved this recipe. The lemon and dill really add a brightness to the squash. I used 2 Tbsp. butter and 1 Tbsp. olive oil. I cooked it at a higher heat for a shorter time so the squash wouldn't get soggy. I also used 1 tsp. dill weed and about 1/4 tsp. each salt and pepper.
This was so good. My 8 yr old and husband both liked it. I think with the amount of butter and dill, you might need to add a few more squash to the recipe. Delicious.

I came across this recipe less than a month ago, and have already made it twice - it's a delicious! The second time I made it, I julienned the zucchini and squash rather than slicing it (so that it would cook a little faster). As some other reviewers have said, it's a lot of butter, so I added an additional big zucchini to the mix, which is the only adjustment I made. And when I removed it from the pan, I cooked some tilapia in the butter/dill mix that remained - it was more than enough. I served it with Far East garlic couscous - the whole meal took about 20 minutes from start to finish. I will make this again and again - maybe next time I will try it with a mix of EVOO and butter to make it even healthier. I really love this recipe!

I was looking for a simple way to enjoy fresh summer squash and this recipe delivered! For more flavor I added two cloves of minced garlic. Delish. If I made it again I would cut a large squash into half-rounds since that's easier to move around the pan for saute. The large rounds I cut did not all get evenly cooked. I like the touch of lemon so next time I think I'd add some lemon slices and a sprig of fresh dill to garnish. To experiment I would also try adding a little white wine to the recipe. And a pinch of sugar.

This was an EXCELLENT recipe- great for the summer as its quick and light and a great way to use up summer squash. I opted for the fresh dill and I would reccomend it this way. Also, I added some asparagus to it. It helped make this "side dish" into a Main course I served over Garlic Cous cous. Very good, thank you!

A wonderful way to let the vegetable taste shine through without all that cheesy goop you usually find on squash! I made this with 3 16-ounce bags of frozen yellow squash. I got many compliments. Everyone thought it was fresh squash. Will make this again and again.
I have made this twice in the last week. First time I followed the recipe, and it was great. Second time I just used all squash and it was equally as good. So easy and so good!!
I followed it exactly and it was delicious! The dill worked so well. Will be making all summer.
Simple and good. I cut down the butter to 3 tbsp instead of 4, I didn’t feel like it was missing anything.
So good!!!!

This is am easy dish to. make if you are in a hurry. It doesn't require anything that would not normally be in your pantry.. It is fairly healthy also. The flavor is so-so. Somewhat bland for my family but you get your veggies in.

Made it just as described. I've always struggled to find a squash recipe that my husband and I both liked. This one delivered. And it's easy and you likely have all the ingredients. Yep, it's a winner.

I sauté zucchini and squash as a side dish quite often since I love it and my boyfriend will eat it, unlike with many other vegetables. This made for the perfect variation. I enjoyed the dill and will make this again. I did use some garlic when sautéing because we love garlic so much. I doubled the recipe for leftovers and used approximately 4 large diced garlic cloves.

Very yummy side dish! I halved this recipe as I was cooking dinner just for my husband and I. Next time I will cut down the butter a bit more. At first I thought it would be too much dill, but it is wonderful with the lemon juice and the veggies. I will definitely make this again!

we both liked this but felt it was a little heavy on the butter.. bf said he'd like to see more lemon so i quadrupled the amount.. it was much improved.. we got to talking and figured it would be better if we could marinate this and then put it on the grill.. we like our veggies a little on the firmer side so less cooking time would be optimal.. the dill was spot on.. ty for the recipe
